note: Self-employed and financially independent — he taught himself to trade well enough to leave a fifteen-year job — and he removed affordability from the table himself: 'I don't have a problem with the price... I don't think that's too much by any means.' Health is unambiguously the neglected area: 80% DoorDash, no training, brain fog, heart racing on a hill. He clears the deconditioned exclusion on history rather than on current state — he is emphatically not gym-averse, having trained daily for over a decade, though no current weight was ever established so the exclusion cannot be tested properly. He misses good_to_great decisively: eight months of deliberate decline means this is a rescue, not an optimisation, and he said as much — 'the second half of me being 39 years old is not good.' Worth noting for the ICP itself: he is the best-qualified prospect in this batch on income and the one who most clearly refused to buy, on grounds the stated criteria do not capture at all — a principle that help must be earned by prior failure.
